title: India: Amazon - Future Group Dispute: Revisiting the Standard of Disclosure in M&A Filings
summary: This article examines the India: Amazon - Future Group dispute, focusing on the standard of disclosure required in M&A filings. It analyzes the Competition Commission of India's (CCI) decision to revoke approval for Amazon's acquisition of a 49% stake in Future Coupons Private Limited (FCPL) due to non-disclosure and suppression of material information, specifically Amazon's strategic intent regarding Future Retail Limited. The piece also suggests regulatory reforms to enhance the transparency and effectiveness of M&A assessments in India, drawing comparisons with disclosure requirements in the US and EU.

title: Firefly Aerospace's Alpha rocket reaches orbit for 1st time
summary: Firefly Aerospace successfully launched its Alpha rocket into orbit for the first time on its second attempt. The rocket deployed three tiny satellites, including one for educational purposes and another from NASA designed for satellite deorbiting. This achievement marks a significant step for Firefly in the competitive small-satellite launch industry.

title: Amazon plans to close several US call centres
summary: Amazon plans to close several call centers in the United States as it encourages customer service employees to work from home. This move, accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic, aims to save money on real estate costs. While transitioning to remote work, Amazon's cloud computing division also offers software for remote customer service.

title: Super Mario Movie toy listings from Jakks Pacific pop up on Amazon
summary: Jakks Pacific is producing an array of Super Mario Movie figures, with listings for Mario, Luigi, Toad, and Bowser already appearing on Amazon. Although no images are available yet, this merchandise will accompany the film's release on April 7, 2023. More toy announcements are expected from various manufacturers as the release date approaches.

title: Jack in the Box seeks full-time Twitch streamer
summary: Jack in the Box is hiring its first-ever full-time Twitch streamer, dubbed "Gamer Jack," to bolster its presence on the Amazon-owned platform. This content creator will host weekly livestreams, develop social media strategies, and collaborate with other streamers to engage with the gaming community. The initiative highlights brands' increasing interest in leveraging creators to reach younger audiences on platforms like Twitch, following similar efforts by competitors such as Hot Pockets and Kellogg's Frosted Flakes.

title: Peloton Bike coming to all Hilton-branded hotels in US by end of 2022
summary: By the end of 2022, all 5,400 Hilton-branded hotels across the U.S. will feature at least one Peloton Bike in their fitness centers, making Hilton the first hospitality brand to offer this widespread access. This partnership also provides Hilton Honors members who are new Peloton users with a free 90-day trial to the Peloton app and preferred pricing on select products. This initiative aligns with Peloton's broader restructuring efforts and recent partnerships to expand its market reach.

title: Trade Desk (Nasdaq:TTD) - Stock Analysis
summary: The Trade Desk (TTD) is currently trading 34.1% below Simply Wall St's fair value estimate of US$29.24, experiencing a challenging period with a 72.6% stock price decline over the past year. Despite strong financial health scores and projected annual earnings growth of 10.65%, the company faces risks such as significant insider selling, executive turnover, client audit concerns, and competitive pressures. Recent news indicates investment in AI and international growth alongside softer near-term guidance.

title: Youngkin’s energy plan calls for reevaluation of Clean Economy Act
summary: Governor Glenn Youngkin unveiled a new energy plan for Virginia, advocating for revisions to the 2020 Clean Economy Act (VCEA) and increased use of nuclear energy, along with greater protections for ratepayers. This plan faces objections from Democratic senators and clean energy advocates, who argue it would hinder Virginia's progress toward clean energy goals and undermine the predictability of its energy system. Youngkin's proposal includes periodic reviews of the VCEA, restoring power to the State Corporation Commission, and addressing electricity rate increases through rate adjustment clauses.

title: How the NetApp/VMware Partnership Benefits Businesses in the Cloud
summary: The partnership between NetApp and VMware aims to help businesses overcome cloud overspending and improve storage solutions. It allows organizations to manage cloud storage consistently, integrate cloud services without major overhauls, and procure storage incrementally based on their needs. This collaboration offers flexibility and cost-efficiency for businesses utilizing cloud environments.

title: Confluent brings designer and governance to streaming data
summary: Confluent has enhanced its cloud platform by introducing new stream designer and advanced stream governance capabilities. These additions aim to simplify the creation and management of streaming data pipelines for organizations using Apache Kafka, making real-time data more accessible and governable. The updates address the growing necessity for real-time responsiveness in businesses and help non-Kafka experts leverage streaming data more effectively.

title: A Giant Supermarket becomes a children’s health center in metro Philadelphia
summary: Nemours Children’s Health is opening a new 19,329-sq.-ft. outpatient pediatric specialty care facility in Broomall, Pennsylvania, within a former Giant Supermarket. This initiative, in partnership with Urban Edge Properties, aims to bring medical care closer to patients in the metro Philadelphia area. The new center, set to open in spring 2023, will offer various medical and therapeutic services, expanding Nemours' presence in southeastern Pennsylvania.

title: Cathie Wood bought up Tesla shares after a Monday stock plunge. They quickly rebounded.
summary: Cathie Wood's Ark Investment Management LLC purchased 132,213 shares of Tesla on Monday, marking her firm's first buy since mid-June after a significant stock decline. This dip-buying activity led to a quick rebound in Tesla's shares by as much as 4% on Tuesday, contributing to S&P 500 gains. The purchase indicates a renewed strategy of buying the dip after a year of selling down her stake in the EV manufacturer, whose shares had previously lost their "crown jewel" status in her main fund.

title: Tupperware selling at Target stores nationwide
summary: Tupperware Brands Corp. announced that its products are now available at Target stores nationwide and on Target's website. This move is part of Tupperware's strategy to "reinvent" itself and reach new customers, particularly younger demographics who may be less familiar with direct sales. The company has also made previous small-scale retail forays with Amazon, HomeGoods, and Bed Bath & Beyond.

title: Coca-Cola Opens West Coast HQ at Spectrum Terrace
summary: The Coca-Cola Co. has opened its new West Coast operations facility at the Spectrum Terrace office campus in Irvine, California. This nearly 10,000-square-foot office will serve as the headquarters for the company's West Zone operations, overseeing over a dozen states and territories. The new space is designed for "connection, collaboration and coaching" for its 125 employees and positions Coca-Cola closer to key markets and customers, including potential partnerships with companies like Amazon, which is also moving into the campus.

title: Amazon (AMZN) Discontinues Glow Video-Calling Device for Kids
summary: Amazon has discontinued its Glow video-calling device for children, launched during the pandemic, due to disappointing sales and changing consumer behavior. The device, which combined a video screen and projector for interactive activities with distant relatives, came from Amazon's Grand Challenge laboratory. This move reflects Amazon's history of experimenting with and sometimes retiring hardware products.

title: Seattle hacker gets probation for $250M Capital One data breach
summary: Paige Thompson, a former Amazon employee, received probation and time served for the 2019 Capital One data breach, which affected over 100 million people and cost the bank more than $250 million. Despite being found guilty of computer and wire fraud, the judge considered mitigating factors including Thompson's transgender identity and mental health issues, leading to a lighter sentence. The Department of Justice expressed disappointment, arguing that the sentence did not reflect justice, especially given that Thompson did not appear to profit from the data or sell it.

title: iShares Russell 3000 ETF IWV
summary: This article provides details on the iShares Russell 3000 ETF (IWV), including its current price, key metrics, and how to invest in it through the eToro platform. It highlights that the ETF aims to replicate the performance of the Russell 3000 Index, encompassing major US companies like Apple, Microsoft, and Amazon. The piece also includes trending ETFs and educational resources on ETF investing.

title: EXEC: Hydro Flask Growth Slows Due To Cautious Buying By Retailers
summary: Hydro Flask's growth has slowed, with market share "down slightly" due to retailers' cautious buying and reduced replenishment amidst concerns about consumer spending slowdown. Despite modest sell-through growth in Q2, strong online sales, and international growth, the brand's overall U.S. market share was impacted. Helen of Troy, Hydro Flask's parent company, lowered its full-year guidance across segments, citing inflation, higher interest rates, and cautious retailer ordering affecting consumer purchasing patterns.

title: Target names Prat Vemana new chief digital and product officer
summary: Target has appointed Prat Vemana, formerly an executive at Kaiser Permanente, as its new chief digital and product officer. He will be responsible for overseeing the retail giant's digital operations. This appointment comes as Target prepares for its October Deal Days and holiday sales period.

title: Seattle software engineer gets probation for 2019 Capital One hack
summary: A former Amazon software engineer, Paige Thompson, was sentenced to five years of probation and time served for the 2019 Capital One hack. Despite prosecutors requesting a seven-year prison sentence, the judge cited her mental health and transgender status as reasons for the probation. Thompson was found guilty of wire fraud and unauthorized computer access but was acquitted of other charges, with the hack affecting over 100 million people.

title: Management Team
summary: This article details the executive management team of Plug Power Inc., including their roles, career histories, and significant achievements. It highlights the leadership's contributions to the company's growth, strategic direction in the hydrogen economy, and operational successes across various departments.

title: Qurate Retail Group names COO
summary: Qurate Retail Group has appointed Scott Barnhart as its new Chief Operating Officer, a move aimed at bolstering its three-year turnaround plan, Project Athens. Barnhart will oversee supply chain, procurement, global business services, corporate real estate, and U.S. customer service and fulfillment operations. This appointment is part of a broader C-suite transformation at Qurate amidst declining sales and a recent downgrade by S&P Global Ratings.

title: As Inflation Rages, Retailers Pump Up Private Label
summary: Amidst rising inflation, retailers are increasingly focusing on developing their private label brands, which are gaining significant market share. While Walmart's private labels reach the most consumers, retailers like Aldi, Target, and Amazon are seeing the fastest growth in household penetration for their own brands. This trend is driven by consumer desire for savings and retailers' pursuit of higher margins and shopper loyalty, impacting purchasing habits across all income levels.

title: AWS is partnering with a concrete company to develop a more sustainable concrete mix for its data centers
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) is collaborating with American Rock Products (ARP) to create a more sustainable concrete mix for its data centers. This partnership has led to a 23% reduction in the carbon footprint of concrete used in new data centers in northeastern Oregon, demonstrating AWS's commitment to achieving net-zero carbon by 2040 and encouraging broader sustainability in the construction industry. The initiative involves extensive data collection, Environmental Product Declarations (EPDs), and the development of low-carbon concrete requirements for AWS facilities.

title: Equinix Expands to Indonesia with $74M Data Center Investment
summary: Equinix, Inc. is expanding its operations to Indonesia with a planned $74 million investment in an International Business Exchange (IBX) data center in Jakarta. This expansion aims to meet the growing digital needs of Indonesian businesses and multinational companies operating in the region, supporting the country's rapid digitalization and its emergence as Southeast Asia's largest digital economy. The new eight-story facility, set to open by the second half of 2024, will offer over 1,600 cabinets and more than 5,300 square meters of colocation space, strategically located in Jakarta's Central Business District.

title: Amazon ends testing of Scout delivery robots
summary: Amazon has ceased testing its Scout home delivery robots, citing that the program was not meeting customer needs despite efforts to create a unique delivery experience. Approximately 400 employees involved in the project will be transitioned to other roles within the company. This decision comes as Amazon continues to invest in other robotics initiatives, including recent acquisitions of iRobot and Cloostermans.

title: Scalable Battery-Electric Van Built for Last-Mile Delivery
summary: The Shyft Group, formerly Spartan Motors, is moving into the electric vehicle market with its new Blue Arc delivery van, designed for last-mile delivery. The company, a major supplier to Amazon, FedEx, and UPS, expects to deliver the vans next summer with pre-orders already being taken. Shyft also developed a portable EV charging system, the Power Cube, to address the long installation times for charging stations.

title: Microsoft, Kyndryl deal connects Azure to IBM mainframe data
summary: Microsoft and Kyndryl have expanded their partnership to facilitate the transfer of mainframe data to Azure, enabling access to AI, web-based analytics, and machine learning capabilities. This collaboration aims to break mainframe data out of its silos by creating secure data pipes between IBM mainframes and Azure, leveraging Microsoft's Power Platform. The deal is seen as a strategic move benefiting both companies and allowing IBM to further its multi-cloud strategy while making mainframe data more accessible for modern application development.

title: Academy Sports’ Debt Ratings Upgraded
summary: S&P Global Ratings upgraded Academy Sports + Outdoors' debt ratings to 'BB' from 'BB-' due to better-than-expected performance, including EBITDA margins of almost 19 percent over the last six quarters. The stable outlook reflects anticipated good performance over the next 12-18 months and stable leverage, despite an uncertain economic environment and competition from larger retailers. Academy's strategic operating initiatives, including improved in-store customer service and omni-channel capabilities, are expected to support long-term growth and maintain strong EBITDA margins.

title: You Don't Need a Membership to Shop at Costco Thanks to These Hacks!
summary: While Costco operates as a members-only club, there are several clever ways for non-members to access their products and services without paying the annual fee. These methods include using the pharmacy, buying alcohol, purchasing from the food court, shopping via Instacart (with a surcharge), or using a Costco Shop Card gifted by a member. Additionally, non-members can shop with a member as their guest.

title: Amazon Abandons Home Delivery Robot Tests in Latest Cost Cuts
summary: Amazon is discontinuing its Scout home delivery robot program, a move that signals the e-commerce giant is scaling back experimental projects due to slower sales growth. The autonomous machine, which had been in testing since 2019, will see its 400-person team disbanded, with employees offered new roles within the company. This decision reflects a shift in focus as Amazon adjusts to current economic conditions.

title: Mizuho Securities to buy 20% of Rakuten Securities for $550 million
summary: Mizuho Financial Group's securities unit will acquire a 19.99% stake in Rakuten Securities for 80 billion yen ($552 million) from Rakuten Group. This strategic move aims to bolster Mizuho's online brokerage business by leveraging Rakuten Securities' expertise and younger clientele. The transaction, expected on November 1st, also helps Rakuten Group raise capital amid competition and significant investments in its mobile network.

title: CVS Health selling benefits technology provider bswift to Francisco Partners
summary: CVS Health is selling its benefits technology provider bswift to Francisco Partners, a global investment firm specializing in technology businesses. While financial terms were not disclosed, bswift will continue its partnership with CVS Health and Aetna. This divestiture comes as CVS Health also engages in acquisitions, such as the recent $8 billion deal for Signify Health.

title: General Electric cuts hundreds of jobs in the U.S.
summary: General Electric is laying off 20% of its onshore wind workforce in the United States, amounting to hundreds of jobs, in anticipation of an economic recession. This move is part of a broader trend among major American companies, including DocuSign, Gap Inc., Meta, Google, Twilio, Patreon, Snap Inc., Apple, Calm.com, Sweetgreen, Groupon, Fender, and Robinhood, which are also reducing their workforces. Companies are citing market realities and the need to streamline operations and improve profitability as reasons for the job cuts.

title: Amazon.com plans to invest over €1 billion in European electric van, truck fleet
summary: Amazon.com announced plans to invest over €1 billion ($974.8 million) in electric vans, trucks, and low-emission package hubs across Europe over the next five years. This investment aims to more than triple its European electric van fleet to over 10,000 by 2025 and acquire more than 1,500 electric heavy goods vehicles. The initiative is part of Amazon's broader commitment to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2040 and to spur innovation in the transportation industry.

title: Why a $158,000 Drug With Unclear Benefits Hurts Whole Health System
summary: The article discusses the implications of the FDA's approval of Amylyx's Relyvrio, a $158,000 drug for ALS, highlighting its unclear benefits and the broader problems it signifies for the healthcare system. It features Layne Oliff, an ALS patient who previously self-medicated with the drug's components for over $7,000 annually, feeling it stabilized his condition. The high price tag and unproven efficacy of such drugs are presented as detrimental to the health system.

title: LivePerson CTO Alan Gilchrest on Humanizing Chatbots and Fighting Bias in AI
summary: LivePerson CTO Alan Gilchrest discusses the evolution of conversational AI, emphasizing its role in humanizing chatbots for customer engagement. He highlights LivePerson's approach to creating world-class AI through extensive data and the 4E Framework for measuring success, while also addressing challenges like personalization without cookies and the ethical importance of fighting bias in AI. Gilchrest believes future advancements will focus on self-healing and self-learning AI to build long-term relationships with machines, advocating for responsible AI governance rather than tricking users into believing they are speaking with a human.

title: Amazon.com to invest over 1 billion euros in European electric van, truck fleet
summary: Amazon announced it will invest over 1 billion euros ($974.8 million) in increasing its European electric van and truck fleet and low-emission package hubs over the next five years. This investment aims to triple its electric van fleet in Europe to over 10,000 by 2025 and purchase 1,500 electric heavy goods vehicles. The initiative supports Amazon's goal of achieving net-zero carbon by 2040 and encourages innovation in the transportation industry by expanding charging infrastructure and micro-mobility hubs.

title: Amazon and clean energy provider to open 19 fueling sites in North America
summary: Amazon and Clean Energy Fuels have partnered to open 19 renewable natural gas (RNG) fueling sites across North America to help reduce greenhouse gas emissions in the trucking industry. The first station opened in Groveport, Ohio, on September 28, with many more expected to be operational by the end of the year. This initiative supports Amazon's goal of using 100% renewable energy by 2025.

title: Some Apple workers in Australia vote to strike over pay, benefits
summary: Australian Apple employees represented by the Retail and Fast Food Workers Union (RAFFWU) have voted to strike on October 18th due to stalled wage negotiations. This planned one-hour strike, involving about 150 of Apple's 4,000 Australian employees, is expected to disrupt services in at least three stores and marks Apple's first strike in the country. The union is demanding wage increases that keep pace with Australia's 7% inflation and guaranteed consecutive weekend days for workers.

title: Amazon's Prime Day-like event kick-starts holiday discount frenzy amid high inflation
summary: Amazon launched its second major sales event of the year, "Prime Early Access Sale," similar to Prime Day, to kick-start the holiday shopping season amidst high inflation. Rival retailers like Walmart, Kohl's, Best Buy, and Target are also offering early discounts to attract customers struggling with squeezed budgets. This early discount frenzy is expected to lead to the slowest pace of U.S. online holiday sales growth since at least 2015.

title: Kohl’s will again keep stores closed on Thanksgiving Day
summary: Kohl's has announced that its stores will remain closed on Thanksgiving Day this year, continuing a practice established in 2020 and 2021. This decision reflects a trend among some retailers to allow employees to spend the holiday with family. The article was written by Sari Lesk for the Milwaukee Business Journal.

title: Timing, vision for new PayPal office in Austin high-rise revealed
summary: Fintech giant PayPal is set to move its Austin operations into Domain Tower 2 early next year. This relocation will place PayPal among other major tech companies like Amazon, Facebook, Indeed, and Vrbo, establishing a stronger presence in Austin's growing tech hub. The article previews details about PayPal's plan to move its employees within Austin, signaling an expansion of its footprint in the city.

title: Walmart’s fulfillment tech expands to Asda stores
summary: Asda, the U.K. grocery chain, will implement Walmart's "Store Assist" app in over 330 of its superstores to enhance in-store picking efficiency. This move is part of Walmart Commerce Technologies' strategy to expand its presence as a technology vendor. The app, built on Walmart's existing fulfillment technology, aims to improve accuracy and speed in omnichannel fulfillment.

title: Invesco Nasdaq 100 ETF: Stash This ETF Away In Your Roth IRA (NASDAQ:QQQM)
summary: This article recommends investing in the Invesco Nasdaq 100 ETF (QQQM) for a Roth IRA, especially given market turmoil. The author highlights why QQQM was chosen over the more common QQQ and discusses its appeal after significant price declines in quality tech stocks like Apple, Amazon, and Microsoft. The author also mentions a collaboration with Hoya Capital for an income-focused investing service.

title: Fox's Tubi touts over 200 streaming channels — but is anyone watching them?
summary: Tubi, Fox Corporation's free ad-supported streaming service, now offers over 200 linear content streams, including news, sports, and general entertainment. Despite an impressive roster of channels and contribution to Fox's $3 billion revenue, a survey by Interpret Research suggests only 20% of Tubi users regularly engage with its linear channels, with the majority preferring on-demand content. Tubi has aggressively pursued local news deals, a strategy differentiating it from competitors like Pluto TV and the Roku Channel.

title: Thermo Fisher buys Mebane facility for $41M, will bring 200 jobs
summary: Thermo Fisher has purchased a property in Mebane for $41 million to establish a new manufacturing base, which is expected to create 200 high-paying jobs in Orange County. This acquisition is part of a multi-million dollar contract with the U.S. government to meet future demand for vital laboratory products. The company has a significant presence in North Carolina with existing facilities and recent acquisitions, including PPD for $17.4 billion.

title: After multiple teen suicides, East Bay company sued for selling deadly chemicals on Amazon
summary: Amazon and an East Bay chemical company, Loudwolf, are facing lawsuits from the families of teenagers who died by suicide after purchasing sodium nitrite from Amazon. The lawsuits allege product liability, negligence, and infliction of emotional distress, claiming the companies facilitated "corporate-assisted suicide" by selling the deadly chemical. Plaintiffs argue that Amazon's platform lacked safeguards to prevent minors from purchasing such substances and even recommended related items for assisted suicide.

title: Comcast Promotes CFO Mike Cavanagh to Added Role of President
summary: Comcast has promoted its Chief Financial Officer, Mike Cavanagh, to the additional role of President, making him the third person to hold this title in the company's 59-year history. Cavanagh will continue as CFO and work closely with Chairman and CEO Brian Roberts to manage Comcast's global businesses. This promotion recognizes his significant operational and financial contributions since joining Comcast seven years ago, following a distinguished career in financial services at JP Morgan Chase and The Carlyle Group.

title: New Convenience-Store Roundup for September 2022
summary: This article provides a roundup of new, and some closed, convenience stores across the U.S. for September 2022. Pennsylvania, Virginia, and Wisconsin each added five new stores, with Sheetz and Kwik Trip opening the most locations overall. In total, 37 new stores opened and one closed, resulting in a net gain of 36 convenience stores for the month.

title: Plan B Entertainment Seeks Buyer, Taps Moelis & Co. to Shop Brad Pitt Production Banner
summary: Brad Pitt's production company, Plan B Entertainment, is seeking a buyer or potential investors and has enlisted Moelis & Co. to explore options. The company, known for critically acclaimed films and TV series such as "The Departed," "12 Years a Slave," and "The Underground Railroad," has a first-look deal with Amazon Studios for TV and an agreement with MGM Studios for film. This move comes as other production companies with strong track records have been selling at high valuations.

title: Microsoft uses strategically located subsidiaries to lower taxes more than previously known, new analysis finds
summary: A new report by the Centre for International Corporate Tax Accountability and Research (CICTAR) alleges that Microsoft uses a network of subsidiaries, particularly in Ireland and Bermuda, to significantly minimize its tax liabilities globally. While not suggesting illegal activity, the analysis raises concerns about profit shifting and its impact on tax revenues in countries where Microsoft conducts substantial business. The report points out that despite high profit margins, some Microsoft subsidiaries report much lower margins, reducing taxable income.

title: Instacart agrees to settle San Diego lawsuit, pay restitution to contractors
summary: Instacart has agreed to a $45 million settlement with the city of San Diego over claims that it misclassified more than 300,000 delivery workers as independent contractors. The lawsuit, initiated in 2019, alleged that Instacart violated California labor laws by not providing benefits and legal protections afforded to employees. The restitution funds will be distributed among delivery workers who worked between September 2015 and December 2020, based on hours worked, with Instacart continuing to deny any wrongdoing.

title: Inspired by Starbucks and Amazon Worker Wins, 300 T-Mobile Customer Service Staff Unionize
summary: Inspired by successful unionization efforts at Starbucks and Amazon, approximately 300 T-Mobile social media customer service workers have formed an independent union, the T-Force Social Care Alliance (TSCA). Citing mass layoffs, pay cuts, and increased work pressure, the TSCA aims to secure protections, economic justice, and job security for its members. This move follows a 2019 merger with Sprint that led to significant job losses at T-Mobile, despite promises of job creation.

title: Albertsons merger with Kroger could be announced this week
summary: Kroger and Albertsons Holdings are reportedly in advanced talks for a merger, with an announcement potentially coming this week. The all-cash acquisition would combine two of the largest supermarket operators in the U.S. This development comes as the grocery industry faces increased competition and demand for updated services.

title: Netflix to get Nielsen ratings as streaming giant rolls out ad-supported plan
summary: Netflix will begin using Nielsen ratings for its ad-supported plan in the U.S. starting in 2023, offering advertisers better insights into audience reach. This move coincides with the launch of Netflix's $6.99 monthly ad-supported tier in November, aimed at boosting revenue after recent subscriber losses. Other streaming services like Amazon Prime and Disney+ also offer ad-supported plans, with varying price points and advertisement loads.

title: Kroger To Buy Albertsons, Creating Grocery Giant
summary: Kroger and Albertsons are reportedly in merger discussions that would unite the two largest supermarket chains in the U.S. Kroger announced on Oct. 14 that it is acquiring Albertsons for $24.6B, assuming $4.7B of Albertsons’ debt, in a deal that would create a grocery giant but likely face antitrust review. The companies plan to divest stores in overlapping markets to facilitate regulatory approval.

title: EXEC: Columbia Sportswear Aims To “Double Down” On Wholesale Growth
summary: Columbia Sportswear plans to intensify its focus on wholesale growth, contrasting with many other brands shifting to direct-to-consumer models. The brand's strategy emphasizes expanding partnerships with key retailers like Dick's Sporting Goods and Amazon, while also leveraging its digital platform, Columbia.com, for brand storytelling and consumer engagement. Columbia aims for significant growth across various regions, targeting a 7 to 9 percent compound annual growth rate over the next three years, with particular focus on Canada, Europe, and China.

title: Kroger has to win over Wall Street and Washington on its Albertsons deal – here's how it plans to do that
summary: Kroger faces the challenge of gaining approval from investors and federal regulators for its $24.6 billion acquisition of Albertsons. The company argues the merger will lower food prices for consumers, increase profitability, and accelerate innovation, while addressing regulatory concerns by divesting 100 to 375 stores. Kroger emphasizes benefits such as significant cost savings, improved shareholder returns, enhanced data opportunities, and better store experiences for shoppers, including lower prices and fresher produce.

title: Solving customer problems in real-time with at NetApp Cloud Field Day Exclusive
summary: This article discusses the second part of NetApp's Cloud Field Day Exclusive, focusing on real-world solutions for hybrid and multicloud challenges. It highlights how NetApp addresses customer pain points like skill gaps, complexity, cost optimization, and consistency in diverse cloud environments. The day also included a Q&A session with Google Cloud executives, discussing the partnership and the future of cloud file storage.

title: Update: the SmartThings Hub and Matter
summary: Samsung has provided an update on Matter features for the SmartThings Hub, clarifying which hub generations will support Thread and how they will interact with other Matter ecosystems. While 3rd generation hubs will gain Thread support and act as border routers, older models will require a separate border router for Thread devices. Initially, the SmartThings hubs will not function as a Zigbee bridge for other Matter environments, but Samsung is deepening integration with Google Home for multi-admin control.

title: Kroger and Albertsons plan merger to combine 2 largest supermarket chains
summary: Kroger plans to acquire Albertsons in a $24.6 billion deal, merging the two largest U.S. grocery chains. The merger is expected to face intense scrutiny from federal regulators and critics due to concerns about competition and soaring food costs. The companies plan to invest savings in price reductions for customers and increased wages for workers.

title: Kroger, Albertsons to Merge in Bid to Create Grocery Giant
summary: Kroger and Albertsons announced a $20 billion merger agreement, including the assumption of $4.7 billion in Albertsons' debt, aiming to create a grocery giant better able to compete with Walmart and Amazon. The deal, which values Albertsons at $34.10 per share, is expected to face significant antitrust scrutiny due to concerns over high food price inflation and market concentration. If approved, the combined company would control about 13% of the U.S. grocery market and anticipates investing in price reductions, store updates, and employee wages.

title: Grocery Store Mega Merger: Ralphs parent company Kroger to buy Albertsons for $20 billion
summary: Kroger has announced its acquisition of Albertsons Companies Inc. for $20 billion, plus the assumption of $4.7 billion in debt, aiming to better compete with major players like Walmart and Amazon in the grocery market. The merger is expected to generate $1 billion in annual savings, which Kroger plans to reinvest into lower prices, higher wages, and improved stores. This deal, however, will face significant scrutiny from U.S. antitrust regulators due to concerns about high food price inflation and potential market concentration.

title: Argentine Ex-President Bemoans Brain Drain, Loss of ‘Our Jeff Bezos’ to Uruguay
summary: Former Argentine President Mauricio Macri criticized the current government's policies, claiming they led to a "brain drain" and the departure of successful entrepreneurs like MercadoLibre founder Marcos Galperin to Uruguay. Macri stated that policies should incentivize wealth creation by individuals, comparing Galperin to Jeff Bezos and emphasizing that politicians should facilitate rather than hinder economic growth. He highlighted that other Argentine entrepreneurs have also moved to Uruguay, citing unpredictability in Argentina as a major factor, rather than just taxes.

title: Kroger Buys Albertsons for $24.6B In Largest Supermarket Merger
summary: Kroger announced its plan to acquire Albertsons for $24.6 billion, a merger that would create one of the largest grocery chains in the United States, second only to Walmart in market share. The deal, expected to close by late 2024 if approved, faces significant scrutiny from antitrust regulators and criticism from labor and consumer advocates who fear potential price hikes amidst high inflation. Both Kroger and Albertsons' shares dropped following the announcement of the acquisition.

title: Kroger and Albertsons Plan $25 Billion Supermarket Merger That May Face Hurdles (Published 2022)
summary: Kroger announced its plan to acquire Albertsons for $24.6 billion, creating a supermarket giant with over $209 billion in annual revenue and approximately 5,000 stores. The merger aims to compete more effectively with big-box retailers like Walmart and Amazon, potentially passing on up to $500 million in savings to customers. However, the deal quickly drew criticism from consumer advocates and politicians concerned about reduced consumer choice, higher prices, and increased corporate concentration in the grocery market.

title: Kroger to buy Albertsons in $24.6 billion deal
summary: Kroger has agreed to acquire Albertsons in a deal valued at approximately $24.6 billion, with the transaction expected to close in early 2024 pending regulatory approval. This merger aims to create a supermarket chain capable of competing with major non-grocery retailers like Walmart and Amazon, leveraging increased scale for better supplier negotiation and operational efficiencies. Regulatory scrutiny is anticipated due to significant market overlap and potential concerns about stifling competition and increasing food prices.

title: Gerbes parent company Kroger intends to buy Albertsons for $25 billion
summary: Kroger announced its intention to acquire Albertsons in a nearly $25 billion deal, aiming to create one of the largest grocery store chains in the United States and boost its scale against competitors like Amazon and Walmart. The merger, expected to close in 2024, faces significant antitrust scrutiny from regulators, consumer watchdogs, and unions, despite plans to spin off nearly 400 stores. Kroger anticipates using half a billion dollars in cost savings from the merger to invest in lower prices amid high food inflation.

title: 5 things to know about Kroger, which plans to merge with Idaho’s largest company
summary: Kroger and Albertsons announced plans to merge, making Kroger Idaho's largest company. Kroger, the nation's largest traditional grocery retailer, operates under many different brand names and is investing heavily in e-commerce. Despite its size and profitability, Kroger has faced criticism for low wages, which it disputes.

title: Target planning 525,000-square-foot warehouse facility in Metro Air Park after $32.4 million land purchase
summary: Target has acquired land for $32.4 million in Metro Air Park to develop a new 525,000-square-foot distribution center. This move follows in the footsteps of competitors Amazon and Walmart Inc., who already operate in the area. Ryan Cos. is involved in the planning of this warehouse project.

title: Corporate Owners of Ralphs, Vons Announce $25 Billion Merger Deal
summary: Kroger and Albertsons have announced a $25 billion merger agreement, creating a mega-chain of approximately 5,000 stores across the nation, pending an antitrust review. While the deal aims to enhance Kroger's competitiveness against Walmart and potentially lower consumer costs, it also raises antitrust concerns for federal regulators. The combined company plans to divest between 100 and 375 stores into a new standalone company to allay these concerns.

title: How Will Kroger’s $25 Billion Buyout of Vons Parent Company Affect Pasadena?
authors: ['CITY NEWS SERVICE WITH PASADENA NOW STAFF']
summary: Kroger's proposed $25 billion acquisition of Albertsons, the parent company of Vons, is currently under antitrust review. This merger would create a massive grocery chain with nearly 5,000 stores nationwide. While the deal could lead to lower costs for consumers and increased competitiveness against Walmart, it raises concerns among workers and analysts about potential monopolies and store closures, especially in areas like Pasadena where both companies already have a significant presence.

title: Amazfit、最新スマートウォッチ「Amazfit GTR 4＆GTS 4」発売
summary: Amazfitは、最新スマートウォッチ「Amazfit GTR 4」と「Amazfit GTS 4」を発売しました。これらのモデルは、業界初のデュアルバンド円偏波GPSアンテナテクノロジーを搭載し、高精度な測位を実現しています。また、150種類のスポーツモードやBioTracker 4.0 PPG生体光学センサーによる健康モニタリング機能、およびスマートウォッチ本体に音楽を保存し再生できる機能を備えています。

title: Lionsgate Signs Worldwide TV Distribution Chief Jim Packer To Long-Term Deal
summary: Lionsgate's President of Worldwide Television Distribution, Jim Packer, has signed a long-term extension to his employment agreement. Under Packer's leadership, Lionsgate has nearly doubled revenues from its film and television library, reaching almost $800M last year. This extension comes as Lionsgate considers spinning off its studio and as its international streaming service, Starzplay, rebrands to Lionsgate+.

title: How one decision, made last year, saved Sea Ltd. from a brush with bankruptcy
summary: Sea Ltd.'s 2021 decision to raise US$6.3 billion in funding, despite having significant cash reserves, proved crucial for its survival. This preemptive move provided a financial runway that allowed the company to weather substantial losses from Shopee's operations and a subsequent market downturn. The article credits CEO Forrest Li's foresight for making a decision that saved the company from potential bankruptcy, highlighting the importance of leadership in navigating unpredictable market conditions.

title: Gartner Top 10 Strategic Technology Trends for 2023
summary: Gartner has identified the Top 10 Strategic Technology Trends for 2023, which are categorized into four key priorities: Optimize, Scale, Pioneer, and Sustainable Technology. These trends aim to help organizations enhance resilience, improve productivity, engage customers, and pursue sustainable solutions. The article details each of the ten trends and their potential impact on business strategies over the next three years.

title: Pardon the Disruption: The digital forces driving the Kroger-Albertsons merger
summary: The proposed $24.6 billion merger between Kroger and Albertsons aims to create a new "Big 3" in the grocery industry, competing more effectively with Walmart and Amazon. Beyond increasing store footprint and negotiating power, the deal is largely driven by the need for scale in data, e-commerce, and retail media, crucial for future profitability and innovation. The merger faces significant regulatory scrutiny regarding potential impacts on competition and prices, with Kroger preparing to divest numerous stores to gain approval.

title: JBG Smith Plans Mixed-Use DC Asset Near Amazon HQ
summary: JBG Smith has revealed plans for the RiverHouse neighborhood, a 36-acre mixed-use project in Arlington, Va., near Amazon's HQ2. The development will include thousands of residential units (apartments, senior living, townhomes, condos), 30,000 square feet of retail, and over 7 acres of public parks. The project plans to redevelop existing parking lots with below-grade garages and enhance connectivity with public transport access and a protected cycle track.

title: Kroger-Albertsons merger: Many views, many angles
summary: The proposed $24.6 billion merger between Kroger and Albertsons faces significant regulatory hurdles but is seen by some analysts as a strategic move to compete with retail giants like Walmart and Amazon. The deal has garnered diverse reactions from various stakeholders, including Wall Street analysts, independent grocers, and organized labor, who express concerns about market dominance, job security, and consumer choice. The merger, if approved, would create a supermarket behemoth with nearly 5,000 stores across 48 states and D.C., leading to potential store divestitures and increased market concentration.

title: What the Kroger-Albertsons merger means for the retail media landscape
summary: The proposed merger between Kroger and Albertsons, valued at $24.6 billion, poses a significant shift in the retail media landscape by combining their first-party data and expanding their retail footprint. This consolidation could allow the new entity to challenge major players like Walmart in the retail media space, offering brands a more compelling advertising platform with a broader reach and richer data for ad targeting. Experts suggest this merger will highlight the growing importance of physical stores and data scale in the future of retail media, potentially benefiting the combined company in a challenging economic environment.

title: スマートウォッチ「Amazfit Band 7」を着けて運動してみたら、厳しい評価に驚き　運動習慣をつけるきっかけに - Fav-Log by ITmedia
summary: The article reviews the Amazfit Band 7 smartwatch, focusing on its utility for exercise and fitness tracking. The author, initially surprised by some "harsh" evaluations from the device, found it to be a catalyst for developing better exercise habits. The review covers the watch's 120 sports modes, automatic exercise recognition, and the detailed data provided through the accompanying Zepp app, highlighting its potential to support new and experienced exercisers alike.

title: Kroger Bets $25 Billion on Bulking Up to Be More Like Walmart
summary: Kroger is making a $24.6 billion bid to acquire Albertsons, aiming to compete more effectively with Walmart and Amazon by investing in lower prices, enhanced technology, and data utilization. The merger faces significant antitrust scrutiny from the U.S. Federal Trade Commission, as critics and analysts debate its potential effects on consumer prices, competition, and the retail landscape. Despite regulatory hurdles and immediate stock drops for both companies, Kroger asserts the deal will ultimately benefit customers through price reductions and improved services.

title: Amazon Helps Ukrainians Gain New Skills and Launch Tech Careers
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) launched "IT Skills 4U," a free workforce-development program aimed at helping Ukrainians pursue careers in cloud computing. The program, available virtually and in Poland, addresses the challenges faced by over 7.5 million Ukrainians who have fled their homes. More than 30 AWS customers and partners, including EPAM Systems, have committed to offering jobs, internships, and traineeships to program participants.

title: Oracle Cloud adds NVIDIA chips, software to speed enterprise AI uptake
summary: Oracle has expanded its partnership with NVIDIA to integrate tens of thousands of NVIDIA's AI-processing graphics chips and software tools into Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). This aims to accelerate enterprise AI adoption across industries like banking, healthcare, and manufacturing by offering powerful A100 and upcoming H100 GPUs. The collaboration will also provide access to NVIDIA software like RAPIDS Accelerator and Clara for enhanced AI performance, medical imaging, and drug discovery.

title: Despite late entry, analysts bullish on Spotify's audiobook play
summary: Analysts are optimistic about Spotify's recent entry into the audiobook market, despite its late start. Although Spotify's audiobook store, launched after acquiring Findaway World LLC, currently has limitations like web-only purchases and U.S.-only availability, experts believe the company can leverage its success in podcasts and the overall growth of audiobooks to compete with established players like Audible. However, challenges remain, including complex licensing for audiobooks compared to podcasts and a flattening growth curve after the pandemic boom, along with Spotify's continued unprofitability despite revenue growth.

title: Could refusing to return to office mean a layoff? Job market's shifting tide may change the rules.
summary: A cooling job market is empowering employers to increasingly mandate a return to the office, shifting the bargaining power from employees. While many businesses still struggle to find workers, this trend is expected to accelerate, potentially leading to layoffs for those who resist office mandates. Some companies are even using return-to-office policies as a way to reduce headcount without official layoffs, as non-compliant employees may choose to quit.

title: Configure Hybrid Cloud with FSx for NetApp ONTAP and VMware Cloud on AWS SDDC using VMware HCX
summary: This article details how to set up a hybrid cloud environment using FSx for NetApp ONTAP as an NFS datastore for VMware Cloud on AWS (VMC) and how to migrate virtual machines from on-premises to VMC SDDC using VMware HCX. It provides a seven-step guide for deploying and configuring HCX, including network and compute profiles, service mesh creation, and demonstrating bulk migration. The integration aims to simplify hybrid cloud deployments, reduce TCO, and enable various migration mechanisms.

title: Tripadvisor Pilots New Limited Series, The Wanderer, on Prime Video
summary: Tripadvisor has launched "The Wanderer," a new limited series on Prime Video, created by its in-house content studio, Wanderlab. The series features experience seekers exploring global destinations, with its first episode focusing on Türkiye in partnership with the Türkiye Tourism Promotion and Development Agency. This initiative provides high-impact exposure for destinations and leverages Tripadvisor's traveler intent data to create unique travel guides.

title: Battle with Bots Prompts Mass Purge of Amazon, Apple Employee Accounts on LinkedIn
summary: LinkedIn experienced a significant purge of fake employee accounts for companies like Amazon and Apple, with some firms seeing a 33% to 50% drop in listed employees overnight. The purges are believed to be LinkedIn's attempt to combat the proliferation of AI-generated profiles and fraudulent activity, including "pig butchering" scams and identity theft. This event highlights a larger problem of bot accounts and raises questions about the accuracy of LinkedIn's employee statistics and its broader impact on the platform's reliability for hiring and networking.

title: Cramer's lightning round: State Street is a buy
summary: Jim Cramer conducted his "lightning round" on "Mad Money," offering quick takes on several stocks. He recommended State Street Corp as a buy, but advised against Novavax Inc and Generac Holdings. Cramer also expressed a general disinterest in media stocks, favoring tech giants like Google, Meta, and Amazon instead.

title: Hawaiian Airlines Announces Agreement with Amazon to Operate Freighter Aircraft
summary: Hawaiian Airlines (NASDAQ: HA) has announced an agreement with Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) to operate an initial fleet of 10 Airbus A330-300 freighters starting in fall 2023. Hawaiian will maintain and fly these aircraft under its FAA certificate to transport cargo for Amazon, with the fleet expanding through 2024 and potentially beyond. This partnership will lead to the establishment of a pilot base on the continental U.S., growth of maintenance bases, and the hiring of additional staff, while Amazon receives warrants to acquire up to 15% of Hawaiian's common shares.

title: Chinese internet giants gear up for global e-commerce push
summary: Chinese e-commerce companies are increasingly looking to overseas markets for growth due to tightening domestic regulations, slowing revenue, and a plateauing user base. Pinduoduo's new cross-border platform, Temu, targets the US market with a low-price strategy, while established players like Alibaba and JD.com are expanding their international retail and logistics operations. Despite geopolitical and economic uncertainties, these tech giants are investing heavily in global expansion, adapting strategies to navigate new challenges like increased compliance demands and supply chain disruptions.

title: Pay cuts push 300 T-Mobile customer service reps to form union
summary: Approximately 300 T-Mobile customer service representatives have formed a union, the T-Force Social Care Alliance (TSCA), in response to pay cuts and potential layoffs. The union aims to secure better working conditions, contrasting with the parent company Deutsche Telekom's unionized environment in Germany. This move follows a period of significant job losses after the T-Mobile-Sprint merger and dissatisfaction with management's handling of compensation.

title: Will my grocery store close? Here’s what a Kroger-Albertsons merger could mean for California
summary: A proposed $24.6 billion merger between Kroger and Albertsons could significantly impact California grocery shoppers and workers. The deal, which involves major California brands like Ralphs, Safeway, and Vons, faces scrutiny from antitrust regulators and concerns from unions and community advocates about potential store closures, job losses, and the creation of "food deserts," especially given the troubled history of the 2015 Albertsons-Safeway merger.

title: UPS hikes 2023 GRI by 6.9%, matching FedEx
summary: UPS announced a 6.9% increase to its 2023 general rate increase (GRI), matching the earlier announcement by FedEx. This increase applies to its U.S. air, ground, and international delivery services, taking effect on December 27, 2022. The move reflects efforts by both carriers to offset elevated cost inflation, with GRIs now serving as a key indicator for contract rates and discounts.

title: Sally Beauty Introduces bondbar: Bond Repair for All Hair Types
summary: Sally Beauty has launched "bondbar," a new line of pro-quality, accessibly priced bond repair products designed for all hair types. The four-step system, born from Sally Beauty's expertise in hair care, aims to address hair damage from styling and coloring, offering clinically proven performance with up to 70% reduced breakage. The products are cruelty-free, vegan, and free of SLS/SLES, parabens, and phthalates, with recyclable packaging.

title: John Deere Tasks Satellite to Connect New Frontiers in Agriculture
summary: John Deere is seeking satellite connectivity solutions to provide always-on internet for thousands of its agricultural machines, especially in rural areas lacking cellular coverage. This initiative aims to unlock the full potential of autonomous farming and advanced real-time data analysis, which could represent a $150 billion incremental addressable market. The company is open to partnerships and believes the volume of machines needing connectivity could open new economic opportunities for the satellite industry, despite challenges in reducing terminal costs.

title: Apple (AAPL) Hikes Music and TV+ Prices in First Increases Since Launch
summary: Apple Inc. has raised the prices for its Apple Music and TV+ services for the first time since their launch, citing increased licensing costs. Apple Music for individuals will now cost $10.99 per month, while Apple TV+ increased by $2 to $6.99 monthly. This price hike makes Apple Music more expensive than rival services from Spotify and Amazon, potentially giving competitors an advantage.

title: Donna James Leads the Plan to Guide Victoria’s Secret into an Inclusive, Profitable Future
summary: Donna James, the board chair of Victoria's Secret & Co., is leading the company's transformation towards inclusivity and profitability after its split from L Brands. With a strong track record as a C-suite executive and business adviser, James is navigating Victoria's Secret through a multipronged effort to remake its image, focusing on diversity, women's advocacy, and addressing past controversial issues regarding body image and financial ties. Her leadership has been crucial in guiding the brand's strategic redirection and fostering a more engaging and accountable internal culture.

title: Amazon Offers Customers a New Way to Pay This Holiday Season With Venmo—a Convenient, Easy-to-Use, and Secure Payment Option
summary: Amazon announced that it will offer Venmo as a new payment option for orders placed on Amazon.com and the Amazon mobile app, starting with select customers and rolling out to all U.S. customers by Black Friday. This initiative aims to provide more convenient, secure, and flexible payment choices for holiday shopping, leveraging Venmo's nearly 90 million users. The transactions will be protected by Amazon's existing security measures and Venmo Purchase Protection for eligible purchases.

title: Mortgages in Walmart – what’s behind the relationship?
summary: Lenders One Cooperative has launched its first in-store mortgage branch locations within select Walmart stores in Florida and New Jersey, aiming to provide easier access to mortgage origination services for shoppers. This initiative is unique, as other major retailers have not pursued similar programs. The strategy leverages Walmart's high customer traffic and trusted brand to connect potential borrowers with loan officers for face-to-face assistance and education.

title: JPMorgan Chase teams with Vera Whole Health to open primary care clinics for employees
summary: JPMorgan Chase is launching primary care clinics for its employees in the Columbus, Ohio area, partnering with Vera Whole Health and Central Ohio Primary Care. This initiative will offer comprehensive in-person and virtual health services to over 20,000 employees and their families, with Morgan Health, JPMorgan Chase's healthcare arm, playing a key role. The move aims to provide high-quality and integrated healthcare, building on Morgan Health's prior investment in Vera Whole Health.

title: Opinion: This one stock stands out when looking at key data from the FAANG+ group
summary: This article discusses the current landscape for tech-oriented stocks, noting that 2022 has been difficult for the sector. It suggests that smart long-term investors should look for bargains among quality merchandise, particularly within the FAANG group. The piece aims to identify one stock from this group that offers a good combination of low valuation and high growth, despite the challenging market conditions.

title: The North Face Five-Year Global Expansion Plan Includes 300 New Stores
summary: The North Face has announced a five-year global expansion plan to open up to 300 new retail and partner locations, while also updating existing stores. This strategy aims to create more experiential shopping journeys with community and educational events, and enhance omnichannel options like BOPIS and ship-from-store. The company seeks to connect with customers on a deeper level through consistent and welcoming experiences across all its physical touchpoints.

title: Creepy deepfake of Elon Musk tied up and held hostage goes viral
summary: A deepfake video of Elon Musk tied up and held hostage, created by reAlpha Tech Corp as an advertisement, has gone viral. The real-estate startup aims to get Musk's attention to join their board, highlighting the growing concern over convincing deepfakes and their ethical implications, further underscored by Scarlett Johansson's past experiences. The video also features a photoshopped Jeff Bezos.

title: Family Feud: National CineMedia Sues Regal For Breach Of Contract, Says Theater Chain Is “Weaponizing” Chapter 11
summary: National CineMedia (NCM) is suing Regal Cinemas for breach of contract, alleging that Regal is using its Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing to improperly terminate a longstanding agreement. NCM claims Regal's parent company, Cineworld, is "weaponizing" the bankruptcy process to resell NCM's exclusive advertising rights to a competitor, jeopardizing NCM's business model and capital structure. Cineworld, however, argues that the existing contract hinders its ability to maximize advertising revenue and that NCM's financial instability necessitates finding a new solution.

title: CouponFollow Celebrates Launch of its Cashback Program with Double Cashback Offers Day
summary: CouponFollow has launched a new cashback program, allowing shoppers to earn cashback at over 1,000 merchants. To celebrate, the company is holding a Double Cashback Offers Day on November 11th, coinciding with the holiday shopping season. This initiative aims to help consumers combat inflation by providing additional savings opportunities through cashback rewards alongside their existing coupon services.

title: Clorox recalls cleaning products that could contain bacteria
summary: The Clorox Company has recalled scented multi-surface cleaners and all-purpose cleaners due to potential bacterial contamination, including Pseudomonas aeruginosa, which can cause serious illness in individuals with compromised immune systems. The recalled products were sold nationwide at various major retailers and online, with specific date codes indicating affected batches produced between January 2021 and September 2022. Consumers are advised to dispose of the products and contact Clorox for a refund.

title: Alamo Drafthouse Cinema opens in Crystal City
summary: Alamo Drafthouse Cinema has officially opened its nine-screen, 915-seat location in Crystal City, near Amazon's second headquarters. This opening comes over five years after the chain initially signed on to anchor JBG Smith's Central District retail development. The article notes the significant changes that have occurred in the area since the initial agreement.

title: Silicon Labs CEO Transforms Company to IoT Chip Designer
summary: Silicon Labs CEO Matt Johnson is transforming the company into a "pure-play" IoT chip designer, focusing solely on wireless connectivity and IoT devices. The company aims to become the undisputed leader in this space, having doubled its revenue in two years and being an early adopter in unifying various IoT standards like Matter, Zigbee, and Zwave. Despite facing competition from larger players and a recent softening of demand, Johnson sees significant growth potential, particularly in areas like digital retail labels and secure hardware.

title: iShares S&P 100 ETF OEF
summary: This article provides current pricing and key metrics for the iShares S&P 100 ETF (OEF), highlighting its stability and offering guidance on how to invest through eToro. It details that OEF aims to replicate the S&P 100, comprising 100 top US companies like Apple and Microsoft. The piece also includes a section on trending ETFs and educational resources for investors.

title: Amazon predicts sales growth slowdown for holidays, crushing shares
summary: Amazon anticipates a significant slowdown in sales growth for the upcoming holiday season, prompting investor concern and an approximately $140 billion drop in its market capitalization. The company attributes this outlook to inflation-wary consumers and businesses tightening their spending, leading to lower-than-expected third-quarter net sales and a cautious approach to future growth. This mirrors a broader trend in the retail and tech sectors, with cloud-computing rivals also facing challenges amidst slowing economic conditions.

title: AMZN Earnings: All you need to know about Amazon’s Q3 2022 earnings results
summary: Amazon.com, Inc. reported its Q3 2022 earnings with net sales increasing 15% year-over-year to $127.1 billion, and net income at $2.9 billion. While earnings surpassed estimates, revenue fell short, and lower-than-expected Q4 guidance (sales projected between $140-148 billion) led to a 20% stock drop in after-market hours.

title: Brief: Trigo nabs $100m, plans expansion of its Amazon Go-like cashierless checkout tech
summary: Israeli startup Trigo has secured $100 million in equity financing, led by Temasek and 83North, to expand its cashierless checkout technology across Europe and the US. The "EasyOut" system, similar to Amazon Go, uses AI and computer vision to enable customers to shop and leave without traditional checkout, while its StoreOS software manages inventory. Trigo plans to deepen its relationships with existing partners like Tesco, ALDI Nord, and REWE Group, and develop new offerings.

title: Jeff Bezos on Brink of $23 Billion Wealth Drop, Among Worst On Record
summary: Jeff Bezos is facing a potential $23 billion reduction in his net worth following Amazon's projection of sluggish holiday sales, which caused the company's shares to plunge. This decline could mark one of the largest single-day wealth drops on record for the Amazon founder. Amazon's stock fell as much as 21% in after-hours trading.

title: Which stocks are moving after the closing bell on Thursday?
summary: This article identifies top gainers and losers in the US stock market's after-hours session on Thursday, October 27, 2022. It lists specific companies like ALFI INC, VERSUS SYSTEMS INC, and PINTEREST INC- CLASS A as top gainers, and AMAZON.COM INC, PTC THERAPEUTICS INC, and VISIONARY EDUCATION TECHNOLO as top losers, with commentary on recent performance and earnings releases.

title: Can Walgreens help Abercrombie achieve its ‘digital revolution’?
summary: Abercrombie & Fitch is expanding its fulfillment capabilities by allowing customers to pick up online orders at approximately 12,000 locations, including Walgreens, FedEx, and Office Depot, as part of its "enterprise-wide digital revolution." This move aims to provide convenient and secure product delivery options and improve the omnichannel shopping experience, building on the company's strong online sales. While some experts question the brand alignment with Walgreens, others see it as a smart strategy to overcome A&F's limited store footprint and increase reach.

title: Chris Gondran of Home Bank - How to Protect Yourself and Your Assets from Cybersecurity Thieves
summary: Chris Gondran, Senior Vice President at Home Bank, offers critical advice on protecting digital assets from cybercriminals, emphasizing strong password practices, vigilance against social engineering scams (phishing, vishing, smishing), and the importance of multi-factor authentication and data backups. The article highlights how human error is a major cause of breaches and directs readers to resources like ic3.gov, stopthinkconnect.org, cisa.gov, and haveibeenpwned.com for further protection and reporting.

title: Still the Biggest Skeleton in the Game? (Published 2022)
summary: This article details the enduring popularity and fervent demand for Home Depot's 12-foot Halloween skeleton, affectionately known as "Skelly," since its introduction in 2020. It highlights the efforts of dedicated shoppers, like Nicole and Jared Kebea, who go to great lengths to acquire the $299 decoration, which has become an iconic symbol of Halloween. The piece explores the phenomenon of "Skelly hunts" and the continued hype surrounding the massive decorative skeleton.

title: Plug Power adding jobs locally to deliver green hydro energy worldwide by 2028
summary: Plug Power's Henrietta gigafactory is now at full production, creating new jobs to support the company's goal of supplying 1,000 tons of green hydrogen daily worldwide by 2028. The facility, which manufactures fuel cell stacks and electrolyzers, also serves as a model for future global expansion. Despite supply chain challenges impacting 2022 revenue projections, Plug Power remains committed to its growth in New York and its mission to build the green hydrogen economy.

title: How to Survive a Shipping ‘A-Parcel-Lypse’? Unchain the Supply Chain
summary: Shekar Natarajan, chief supply chain officer at American Eagle Outfitters, warns of an impending "a-parcel-lypse" due to distribution and fulfillment inefficiencies. He advocates for companies to collaborate and share resources to create a more elastic supply chain, rather than each building individual, costly networks that lack the scale of giants like Amazon or Walmart. American Eagle's Quiet Platforms is an example of this approach, offering shared logistics services to over 60 customers to improve efficiency and reduce costs.

title: Peace of Mind Shared in a Photograph: FedEx Launches Picture Proof of Delivery to Bolster E-Commerce Residential Delivery
summary: FedEx Express has launched Picture Proof of Delivery (PPOD) for express residential deliveries in the Asia Pacific region, a new service enhancement to address the growing e-commerce market. This free service provides customers with a photo of their package's exact delivery location, offering peace of mind for both consumers and e-tailers. The initiative aims to digitize services, improve customer experience, and supports the significant growth of the B2C e-commerce market in Asia Pacific.

title: How did the surprise Amazon Prime Day in October 2022 compare to similar sales events?
summary: Amazon's second Prime Day event in October 2022 saw lower sales than the July 2022 Prime Day, but sales were still higher than Prime Day events in 2020 and 2021. The sales growth during Amazon's October event outpaced Walmart and Target's competing sales events. Despite the success of Prime Day, Amazon's weekly sales during these events remain lower than holiday shopping sales in December.

title: Ansys launches latest simulation gateway product powered by AWS
summary: Ansys has partnered with Amazon Web Services (AWS) to introduce its new Ansys Gateway powered by AWS product. This collaboration brings together Ansys's simulation technology with AWS's on-demand cloud computing platforms. The launch is a significant step for Ansys in expanding its product offerings and leveraging cloud infrastructure.

title: Shopify acquires Remix to bolster its storefront design tools
summary: Shopify has acquired Remix, an open-source web framework similar to Next.js, to enhance its storefront design tools. The acquisition will provide Remix with long-term backing from Shopify, allowing it to accelerate growth and improve performance and scalability, with Shopify itself planning to integrate Remix across many projects. This move is expected to benefit developers building on Shopify's Hydrogen framework by addressing challenges in data loading, routing, and error handling.

title: Industry Voice: As Market Dynamics Pivot, Alpha Opportunities Are Set to Improve
summary: The US equity market has seen challenges for active managers due to low volatility, market concentration, and reliance on macro factors and momentum. Historically, however, such extreme market characteristics have often led to improved opportunities for active stock picking and outperformance against passive strategies as these conditions normalize. The article suggests that current market dynamics indicate a potential shift where active management could find more avenues for generating alpha.

title: Naver Webtoon to pursue profits with Yonder app launch in US
summary: Naver Webtoon is launching a new serialized fiction app called Yonder in the US market to replicate its successful Korean business model and improve profitability in overseas operations. The app will feature translated Korean web novel hits and original titles, aiming to create synergy with its acquisition, Wattpad. This move is part of Naver Webtoon's broader strategy to shift from expansion to profitability after facing operating losses in international markets despite user growth.

title: Payoneer to Present at Upcoming Investor Conferences
summary: Payoneer Global Inc. announced its management team will participate in two upcoming investor conferences: Citi’s 2022 FinTech Conference on November 14, 2022, and Credit Suisse’s 26th Annual Technology Conference on November 29, 2022. Investors can access webcasts and replays of the presentations through the Company's investor relations website. Payoneer, a commerce technology company, powers payments and growth for businesses in the digital global economy.

title: ESG Indexes Lifted by Carbon-Efficient Firms but Underperformed
summary: MSCI ACWI ESG Indexes underperformed during the first three quarters of 2022 despite generally outperforming from 2013-2021. While carbon-efficient firms positively contributed to performance, exclusions from the MSCI ACWI ESG Leaders Index due to ESG controversies and significant negative contributions from specific stocks like Apple and Amazon primarily drove the underperformance. Industry factors, particularly energy and aerospace and defense, saw a reversal in performance but played a lesser role in the overall ESG index underperformance compared to stock-specific exclusions and dollar strengthening.
